title: Writing CSV files
summary: csv.writer and DictWriter, quoting done for you, filling missing fields, and filtering one CSV into another.
hints: Open the output with `open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8")`. `write_rows`: `w = csv.writer(f)`, `w.writerow(header)`, `w.writerows(rows)`. The writer quotes fields that contain commas or quotes on its own.

`write_records`: `csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames, restval="", extrasaction="ignore")`, then `writeheader()` and `writerows(records)`. `restval` fills missing keys; `extrasaction="ignore"` drops keys that are not in `fieldnames` instead of raising.

`to_csv_text`: write into `buf = io.StringIO()` with `csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")`, then `return buf.getvalue()`. `filter_csv`: open both files in one `with`, make a `DictReader` and a `DictWriter(dst, fieldnames=reader.fieldnames)`, write the header, then each row where `keep(row[column])` is true, counting as you go.
